title: Virtual Head Attention
summary: VHA replaces standard GQA attention in a model trained from scratch, using a query premix and a low-rank I + AB^T postmix that fold into the query and output projections at inference, yielding a GQA-2-equivalent model with two KV heads. The cost is that the gains only exist if the architecture is adopted at pretraining time; it cannot be retrofitted onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and the reader has no pretraining budget. What can fail after adoption is unvalidated quality at scales or context lengths beyond the reported experiments, and the small accuracy deltas may not transfer to downstream fine-tuning or domain-specific workloads.
rationale: The technique is compelling for long-context serving but requires training a model from scratch, which the reader's constrained infrastructure and reliance on existing checkpoints or APIs preclude.
technique: Virtual Head Attention (VHA) for KV compression

claims.statement: VHA replaces standard GQA attention in a model trained from scratch, using a query premix and a low-rank I + AB^T postmix that fold into the query and output projections at inference, yielding a GQA-2-equivalent model with two KV heads. The cost is that the gains only exist if the architecture is adopted at pretraining time; it cannot be retrofitted onto existing pretrained checkpoints, and the reader has no pretraining budget. What can fail after adoption is unvalidated quality at scales or context lengths beyond the reported experiments, and the small accuracy deltas may not transfer to downstream fine-tuning or domain-specific workloads.

Reduces KV cache by 4x vs. GQA-8 at dense scales and 2x vs. GQA-4 at MoE scale, cuts training/prefill FLOPs by 7.9% (1.7B, S=4096), and matches or exceeds GQA quality (+0.05% to +0.81% across four scales; +0.70% over MLA and +2.60% over GQA-4 on a 30B-A3B MoE 12-benchmark suite; RULER 84.4 vs. 73.0 for GQA at 8K-128K).
